scope: Native cross-document navigation opt-in timing and transition promise lifecycle

environment.probeInput: mobile viewport emulation with touch enabled

firstRecordingAttempt.observedError: Transition was aborted because of invalid state. ViewTransition opt-in disabled

originalDiagnosticProbe.note: This probe did not reproduce the preceding recording failure. It does not invalidate that earlier failure.

beforeFix.preservation: The original failed recording report and original diagnostic output were retained privately and were not overwritten by this retest.

analysis.directlyObserved: The failed receiving document reported opt-in disabled and had no ViewTransition object in pagereveal, while the outgoing document had a transition. The native navigation still displayed the intended page.
analysis.chromiumSourceMatch: The inspected Chromium implementation skips with kRejectInvalidState and kOptInDisabled, then returns null, when the receiving document's cross_document_opt_in_ is disabled. This matches the observed error and missing receiving object.
analysis.timingNotObserved: The original probe did not record the exact external stylesheet download, parse or application time. An external-CSS timing race is the repair hypothesis, not a directly measured cause in that original run.
analysis.promiseBoundary: A skipped transition can reject ready while finished resolves. Handling finished alone does not handle ready rejection, and an incoming event with no transition object cannot be repaired by attaching a later ready handler.

details: Move the sole @view-transition navigation:auto rule into an early inline style in Layout head, before the synchronous preference script and external stylesheet.
Register pageswap and pagereveal preference protection in the synchronous head script and handle each transition's ready rejection before an intentional skip.
Keep the enhancement module's active-transition cleanup and independently settle ready rejection and finished completion.
Keep native anchor navigation, the main-only 220ms arrival animation, static root snapshot behavior and pause/reduced-motion fallback. No global error event suppression was added.

newCases.scenario: Hold the external CSS response during real link navigation. Before releasing it, verify the incoming document already has a parsed inline opt-in; then verify the real transition becomes ready, main uses content-arrival, the root uses no animation, and language navigation still works.

Change the saved pause preference after outgoing handlers run and hold incoming JavaScript modules. Verify the receiving document has a real transition, its head handler calls skipTransition, main has no transition animation, and the pause remains after module release and language navigation. The test does not catch ready itself.

existingCasesRechecked: Native content transition with no background fade
Saved global pause across native navigation
Native history return, card input and both cached/final cleanup branches
targetedRegression.fullSuiteBoundary: This was a six-case targeted run, not the complete 103-case suite. The complete suite is reported separately.

afterFixMobileProbe.method: Replay the original diagnostic sequence in a fresh context for each browser: Chinese homepage, reduced motion on/off, theme tap, screenshot, real Work link tap, screenshot and real homepage brand tap. The probe initializes dark/unpaused storage on each new document, so it is not evidence of theme persistence across navigation.
warningsRetained: Both versions: existing THREE.Clock deprecation warning.
Bundled Chromium: ReadPixels GPU-stall and unsupported KHR_parallel_shader_compile warnings.
afterFixMobileProbe.visualReview: The bundled-browser homepage and Work screenshots were opened and inspected; content remained readable, with no visible horizontal overflow or blank navigation result in these two captures.

evidenceBoundary: This sanitized report contains scoped local browser observations, source-based analysis and test results. Raw timelines, traces and diagnostic screenshots remain private. Two successful probe runs do not establish an exhaustive absence of timing failures. No real-device, deployment or performance claim is made.
